clue.text: Fair with skinhead in residence

indicators.note: the residence word is split open so the other pieces sit within it

parts.note: a residence is a home
with means and, joining things together
the head, or first letter, of the word skin

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed lodger is staying in the house, and someone thinks him good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' looks like a shaven-headed youth, but it means the head of 'skin'; 'with' is a piece, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the old sense means good-looking or attractive, a synonym.

clue.text: A name for being a lady's man?

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to call a ladies' man.
explanation.walkthrough: Split, the name reads as a woman's man.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a masculine first name.

clue.text: In climbing, many see this to advantage

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the word In upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Mountaineers enjoy a good view of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY, a Cambridgeshire cathedral city, is the crossword favourite. 'Climbing' turns IN to NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something well or favourably is doing it to advantage, a synonym.

clue.text: The workshop boss "X"

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud
X is the Roman numeral ten, written 10, which looks like the letters IO

explanation.surface: The foreman of a workshop is known only as X.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is the decorative knob, not a manager; X as ten is read as the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or craftsperson's workroom is a synonym.

clue.text: Union organiser

parts.note: looks like a trade union official, but the union is a marriage and this person arranges it

explanation.walkthrough: The trade-union reading is the trap; the union is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arranges marriages between couples organises a union of two people.

clue.text: Demanding, which is just like the top man!

parts.note: as means in the manner of, just like
a king is the man at the top of a kingdom

explanation.surface: Someone exacting is compared to the boss, who is exacting too.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer says 'like the king', the top man.
explanation.definitionFit: Demanding and this word both describe making a request, as in requesting payment.

clue.text: Firm admitting gold may be stockpiled

indicators.note: admitting means the firm word lets the gold in

parts.note: stable means firm, steady
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A company taking in bullion that might be hoarded.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something able to be kept in reserve or stored is fit to be stockpiled.

clue.text: Annoyed about girl endlessly turning up wet

indicators.note: about means the annoyed word goes round the other piece

parts.note: irate means angry, annoyed

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the trimmed word upwards, so backwards
endlessly removes the last letter of the word girl

explanation.surface: Someone cross because a girl keeps arriving soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' leaves GIR, which 'turning up' makes RIG in this down clue; 'about' wraps the anger word round it. 'Wet' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate land is to water it, to make it wet.

clue.text: With the old monarch even the French is most colourful!

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
e'en is the poetic contraction of even
est is the French word for is

explanation.surface: Someone claims a past king was the most flamboyant of all.
explanation.walkthrough: E'EN is poetic shorthand for 'even'; 'the French' signals a French word, EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is a colour, so the superlative is a playful way of saying most colourful.

clue.text: Producing one's curt reports

indicators.note: producing suggests making something new out of the following letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken with its S, giving the letters ONES

explanation.surface: Someone creates their own short summaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Producing' rearranges the letters of ONES and CURT; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount is to narrate or tell, so the verb means gives reports of.

clue.text: Within the Church rows would appear common

indicators.note: within places the rowing word inside the Church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
oars are what one rows with, and to oar is to row

explanation.surface: Squabbles inside the church would look vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels but here means oars, the verb of rowing; it sits inside CE, the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Common in the sense of vulgar or unrefined is a synonym.

clue.text: Totally in the dark?

parts.note: all means totally, wholly
night is the time of darkness

explanation.surface: Someone is completely ignorant of what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests complete ignorance; the whole clue also describes lasting through every hour of darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting throughout the hours of darkness, like a vigil or a café that never closes, fits the description.

clue.text: Arming maybe, being on edge

indicators.note: maybe says the word arming is only one possible order of these letters

explanation.surface: Getting weapons ready makes someone nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' reads as nervous, but 'edge' alone is the definition and 'being on' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A border or rim of a page or area is a synonym for edge.

clue.text: Far from appreciative of a good tryer unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters of a good tryer are jumbled

explanation.surface: Being dismissive of someone who tries hard is a pity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparaging or belittling remarks are the opposite of appreciative ones.

clue.text: They'll go around places, receiving a tip off

indicators.note: receiving means the places word takes in the other pieces

parts.note: sites are places
to tip off is to tell or inform

explanation.surface: Locations get a warning about something circling them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They'll go around' sounds like visitors touring, but it means orbiting bodies; 'receiving' opens the places word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Moons and artificial spacecraft are bodies that orbit planets.

clue.text: The recreant had a meal after a job of work

indicators.note: after places the eating word behind the job phrase

parts.note: a post is a job
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: A traitor ate after finishing a shift.
explanation.walkthrough: A recreant is a deserter of a faith or cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A recreant is an old word for a traitor or renegade, someone who abandons their faith.

clue.text: Popular pro

explanation.definitionFit: Popular means looked on with approval, and pro means supporting a cause.

clue.text: Taking simpletons in, he's killing!

parts.note: two asses, fools
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fooling the gullible, someone is having a great time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simpletons' is plural, so it gives two ASSes; 'Taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer, especially of a public figure, is one who carries out a killing.

clue.text: Bloomer made by possibly ten postmen

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of ten postmen can be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A howler committed by maybe ten mail carriers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is a flowering plant; 'made by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and this North American garden flower is one.

clue.text: Runs through 21 areas

definitions.meaning: barren, dry regions like those of 21 down

explanation.definitionFit: Squandering money is running through it, and dry barren regions are wildernesses.

clue.text: Covering up for a beating

explanation.definitionFit: Concealment is the act of keeping out of sight, and a thrashing is a sound beating.

clue.text: Abandon land that's too dry to raise crops

definitions.text: land that's too dry to raise crops

explanation.definitionFit: To forsake someone is to abandon them, and an arid wasteland is too dry for farming.

clue.text: Growth which is dull in the main?

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the sea
matt or mat means dull, without shine

explanation.surface: A question about something boring growing in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old literary word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea mat is a colonial marine organism, a growth found on seaweed and shells.

clue.text: Hit back taking a position for a sponger

indicators.note: back means the hitting word is read in reverse

parts.note: a rap is a sharp hit
a site is a position or location

explanation.surface: A retaliation against someone who lives off others by taking up a spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit back' looks like retaliation, but 'back' reverses RAP to give PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeloader who lives off others is a synonym, from the creature living on a host.

clue.text: Turn on a contrivance-there's nothing in it

indicators.note: in it means the zero goes inside the trick word just mentioned

parts.note: a ruse is a contrivance or trick
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Something switched on by a gadget turns out to be empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's nothing in it' sounds like a verdict but puts O inside RUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on is to excite or stir up, a synonym.

clue.text: Having to do with platitudinous penitent

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them, to con them
platitudinous means trite, hackneyed

explanation.surface: Someone sorry is linked with dull clichés.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' here is the slang verb for swindling someone; 'Having' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitent and this word both mean feeling remorse for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Commit a blunder and get the message!

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Make a mistake and then understand what you are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the message' sounds like understanding; 'message' is a task you are sent on.
explanation.definitionFit: A message in older British use is a short trip to deliver or fetch something.

clue.text: Watch what's worth viewing. That makes sense

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
a sight is something worth seeing

explanation.surface: Look at the attractions: it is all reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That makes sense' sounds like agreement; it is a definition of one of the five senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses, so it literally makes up a sense.
